notes: §1985:VI.6.18.3 SR5 limits the operands to one character in level 1 only: "Except as specifically noted in syntax and general rules, this restriction on length does not apply to level 2." The compiler implements the level 2 Nucleus at 85, so the requirement is to accept operands longer than one character: InspectCharOperandOf binds literal-1, literal-2, literal-3 and identifier-3, identifier-4, identifier-5 with no length limit (the lengths the other rules do fix are CheckInspectLiteralSizes for SR7 and SR9 and the CHARACTERS replacement of SR8), and the runtime compares a pattern of any length (RunCycle) and locates a BEFORE/AFTER delimiter of any length (Region). The witness tallies ALL "AB" BEFORE INITIAL "CA" and replaces with two-character identifier-3, identifier-4 and identifier-5 and two-character literals, with the output the general rules require.

next.reason: 1985: "In level 1, literal-1, literal-2, and literal-3, and the data items referenced by identifier-3, identifier-4, and identifier-5 must be one character"; 2023: "No level subsets; one-character limit kept only for CHARACTERS phrase: "literal-3 shall be one character in length" (SR-14.9.22.3-7)". The 1985 rule is a level-1 subset limit requiring one-character INSPECT operands. 2023 has no subsets and requires one character only with the CHARACTERS phrase.
